notes: All 15 merged discovery/diamond records were inspected after applying fee and ranking patches. Official costs, article/review distinctions and selected workflow conditions were independently checked for every record. This is the fifth distinct role review, not human scientific review or editorial acceptance.

Fee outcomes remain 13 verified_free compliant routes and 2 needs_verification. No actual compulsory Sage page fee was found. CMOT has no APC on subscription, but other charges remain unresolved; Network Science has a conditional Gold OA waiver and unresolved submission fee.

Five provisional high bands were replaced with unknown because no anchored cross-venue comparison was established. All 15 final bands are unknown. Contribution hurdles remain relevant fit guidance; absence of a tier never means easy acceptance.

All ranking metrics are preserved without replacement. Reviewer rechecked OSS 6.0%, Acta 12.8% and TSR 18.7% official displays, their missing years/cohort limits, CMOT 2025 values, Sociologia 2025 value/2026 release and Network Science undated citation values/2024 article counts. No check date became a metric year; no publication count became an acceptance denominator.

The Sage policy distinguishes assistive use from generative use and requires human output verification. Its prohibited uses require workflow planning before manuscript preparation; the record warning is a concise pointer, not the complete policy. Source: https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy

Sage expressly welcomes independent researchers while allowing extra integrity checks. Institution-based optional OA agreements are not needed for the cataloged subscription routes. Source: https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/policy-on-submissions-from-independent-researchers

Author affiliation metadata alone was not converted into a mandatory institutional eligibility gate. Where an explicit independent-author or AI policy was not found, the gap is recorded; the review did not test submission-system forms.

Browser retrieval failed for Sociologica and Przeglad pages and Network Science metrics; complete official HTML was then read via ordinary HTTPS with status 200. SSCR live HTML timed out; its publisher-hosted author-instructions PDF was read. No access controls were bypassed.
Only research/review/sociology-organizations.json was written. No submissions, contacts, remote writes, installations or human approval claims were made.
